as_told.title: Five people at the legacy company: engineers, no physicists

plain: Eric Davis, a physicist who has worked on Pentagon studies, says that in the 2010s a senior vice president and materials scientist at an old, established aerospace company told him about the company's program to study crashed craft of unknown origin. Davis says he asked where their physicists were, and the man said they had none, ever, because only a handful of people in the company were allowed to work on it. Davis also says he knew five such people himself, including a woman who was a mathematician but served as chief of security, which, if true, would mean recovered craft were being studied by a tiny team without the experts needed to understand them.
